title: Beatrix and the Gravity
premise: Xanthe Pemberton smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers through the blockaded orbits of the Meridian System, keeping her head down and her past erased. When gravity fails for nine seconds system-wide, she discovers the flicker was a signal — and that a wafer she's been paid to ignore contains coordinates to the weapon that caused it, hidden by a dead courier who trusted no one but a stranger. Hunted by both warring fleets who each want to control or destroy the message, Xanthe assembles an unlikely crew of outcasts to deliver it to the neutral station where both sides' civilians can hear the truth: the war was manufactured by the orbital cartels. She delivers it at devastating personal cost, losing her ship and nearly her identity, but gains the family she never believed she deserved.
about_author: Mara Sandoval is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices cross empty distances. She writes about people who carry things — cargo, secrets, each other — across hostile space.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Mid-run through contested orbit, gravity dies for exactly nine seconds; coffee floats, cargo shifts, and every comm channel screams. When gravity returns, so does a transmission she shouldn't be able to receive. The beat is unease: her carefully invisible life has just been noticed.

chapters.title: The Wafer That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Xanthe inventories her hold and finds one extra memory-wafer, sealed in a courier's cipher she recognizes from her erased past. POV alternates with customs inspector Dae-Ho Okonkwo, who flags her ship. Emotional beat: dread — someone planned this before the flicker.

chapters.title: What the Dead Courier Knew
chapters.summary: Xanthe decodes the wafer's outer layer: a dead man's voice, courier Ilya Voss, naming her and warning that the message must reach Meridian Station before the fleets' next offensive. POV: Xanthe. Beat: reluctant responsibility awakening in someone who swore off causes.

chapters.title: Customs, Corruption, and Coffee
chapters.summary: Dae-Ho boards her ship under pretense of inspection while cartel agents watch. He lets her go — deliberately, she realizes — because he suspects the flicker was no accident either. POV: Dae-Ho. Beat: first fragile alliance between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Engineer Who Lives in the Walls
chapters.summary: Xanthe recruits Juno Reyes, a disgraced fleet engineer squatting in a decommissioned tug, to trace the flicker's origin. Juno confirms it came from inside the cartels' own relay network. POV: Juno. Beat: found family begins forming around shared exile.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Want Her
chapters.summary: A Republic frigate and a Concordat corvette converge on Xanthe's position simultaneously; she escapes by threading a debris field neither will enter. POV: Xanthe. Beat: terror sharpening into defiance — she understands now how valuable she is.

chapters.title: Ilya's Ghost
chapters.summary: Deeper decryption reveals Ilya Voss was Xanthe's mentor before her memory wipe, and that she volunteered to forget him to protect the message. POV: Xanthe, interleaved with Ilya's recorded voice. Beat: grief for a self she chose to lose.

chapters.title: The Neutral Station
chapters.summary: The crew reaches Halcyon Ring, a civilian station where refugees from both sides coexist. They witness what the war actually costs: ration lines, orphaned kids, a memorial wall with too many names. POV: Juno. Beat: the stakes become human, not strategic.

chapters.title: A Price Named Pemberton
chapters.summary: Cartel brokers offer Xanthe her original memories back in exchange for the wafer. She learns her real name, her real crime, and why she erased herself. POV: Xanthe. Beat: temptation — belonging to her own past versus her new crew.

chapters.title: Juno's Mutiny
chapters.summary: Juno, discovering the message could end the war but also expose her own war crimes, tries to destroy the wafer. Xanthe stops her without violence, choosing trust over punishment. POV: Juno. Beat: forgiveness as the glue of found family.

chapters.title: The Cartel's Face
chapters.summary: The crew infiltrates a cartel gala to learn who ordered the flicker: Director Sable Ashwin, who engineered the war to monopolize jump-lane patents. POV: Dae-Ho undercover. Beat: cold clarity — the enemy has a name and a smile.

chapters.title: Running Out of Orbit
chapters.summary: Ashwin puts a bounty on the whole crew; their safehouses burn one by one. They flee toward Meridian Station with both fleets and the cartels closing in. POV: rotating. Beat: desperation binding them tighter than any contract.

chapters.title: The Kid on the Dock
chapters.summary: A stowaway — a refugee girl named Pip who copied part of the wafer — forces the crew to decide whether the message belongs to everyone. They vote yes. POV: Pip. Beat: hope through the eyes of the generation the war broke.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Shoals
chapters.summary: Concordat forces trap them in a navigation shoal; Juno sacrifices the tug's drive core to break free, stranding them on a drifting hulk. POV: Juno. Beat: sacrifice proving loyalty beyond words.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Stranded, Xanthe finally plays the deepest layer of the wafer: her own pre-wipe testimony about the war's manufactured origins — evidence she gathered seven years ago and buried. POV: Xanthe. Beat: reckoning; she was always part of this story.

chapters.title: The Nine-Second Truth
chapters.summary: Dae-Ho defects openly, bringing customs codes that can broadcast the message fleet-wide from Meridian Station's tower. Ashwin's assassins board en route. POV: Dae-Ho. Beat: a bureaucrat choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Assassins breach the hulk; the crew fights together for the first time as a unit, protecting Pip and the wafer. Someone must stay behind to seal the breach. POV: rotating. Beat: family forged in fire.

chapters.title: The Cost of Delivery
chapters.summary: They reach Meridian Station, but broadcasting requires manual override in a radiation-flooded relay spine. Xanthe goes, knowing exposure may erase what remains of her memory again. POV: Xanthe. Beat: willing sacrifice — survival's price made literal.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe transmits Ilya's evidence and her own testimony to every screen in the system during the fleets' final offensive. Weapons stand down mid-volley as crews hear the truth. Ashwin's network collapses. Beat: catharsis — the message lands.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe wakes in Halcyon Ring's infirmary with gaps in her memory but surrounded by faces that refuse to leave. Armistice talks begin; Dae-Ho testifies; Juno turns herself in voluntarily. POV: Pip. Beat: tender aftermath.

chapters.title: Names on the Wall
chapters.summary: The crew adds Ilya Voss's name to the memorial wall and, after debate, Xanthe's old name beside it — honoring who she was without letting it define her. POV: Xanthe. Beat: integration of past and present selves.

chapters.title: Gravity Holds
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, Xanthe pilots a refitted freighter with her chosen family aboard, hauling honest cargo through open lanes. Gravity flickers once — a rumor, a ghost — and no one panics. Beat: earned peace; belonging is no longer contraband.
